title: Hexagonal architecture (ports and adapters), in the software-engineering canon
takes: The core talks to the world only through ports it defines; adapters plug technologies in; in-memory adapters make tests trivial. Paired with functional core, imperative shell, and testing at the seams.

title: GitHub Actions: concurrency groups
takes: Jobs that share a resource take turns; the rest run freely.

title: Crash-Only Software
takes: A system that can be killed at any moment and recovers by reading its own record, the same way every time.

title: Kanban: flow efficiency
takes: Time worked divided by total time, waits included - the share of a job's life spent on it.

title: git worktree
takes: Several working trees from one repository: each job its own, none shared.

title: Healthchecks: a dead man's switch
takes: Alert on absence: silent while pings arrive, alerting when one is late; the watcher lives elsewhere.

title: Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency
takes: An action that changes the world carries a key, so doing it twice finds it done.

title: Kubernetes: Jobs
takes: A finished job is never started again; deadlines and time-to-live end what waits too long.

title: How to do distributed locking
takes: A lease can expire while its holder is paused; a fencing token that only grows lets the resource refuse the stale holder.

title: Patterns of Distributed Systems: Lease
takes: A lease is a lock with a time limit: acquire, renew, release, expire.

title: A Proof for the Queuing Formula: L = λW
takes: Work in flight equals throughput times time in the system: shorter waits, or more work in flight, raise throughput.

title: GNU make: parallel execution (-j)
takes: Run what does not depend on each other side by side; declare what depends on what.

title: The ideal-project playbook: names explain the program; guards
takes: Areas named for what the program is for, not for patterns; tool words only in the adapter that drives them; purity by role, vocabulary and findability checked on every change.

title: Most widely deployed SQL database engine
takes: Embedded, everywhere, and stable for decades: a store and query engine that needs no server.

title: Temporal: durable execution
takes: Every step recorded in an append-only event history; after a crash, resume from the last recorded step without repeating finished ones.

title: Long-running activity: progress and cancellation with heartbeats
takes: A long step heartbeats its progress; a lost worker is noticed within the heartbeat timeout, and the retry resumes from the last checkpoint.

title: Toyota Production System: the seven wastes
takes: Waiting is one of the seven wastes: time in which nothing is made.
